Major Benefit
Elemental Adaptation - You have developed an affinity to an element as well as glands in your hands that can exude a chemical tied to that element.  Pick one of the following elements: Fire, Cold, Lightning, Acid.  You gain resistance to that element.  Spells you cast ignore resistance to damage of the chosen type.  As an action you can apply a secretion from your hands to a weapon (or 20 pieces of ammunition).  For the next minute, items you applied it to do an additional 1d4 damage of the element type.  If anyone that is not you uses these items, they take 1d4 damage when they pick up the weapon, and at the beginning of each of their turns.

Major Detriment
Death’s Door - Your features become ashen, sunken, more zombie like.  You lose half your hit dice (specifically the ones you would have gotten on your even levels).  In addition, you only get a hit die when you gain an odd numbered level.  You succeed death saving throws only with a roll of 15+, and a natural 20 on a death saving throw only counts as 1 success and has no other effects.  Lastly, if anyone turns undead within your sight, you must make the saving throw too, and immunity to fear doesn’t prevent you from being turned.

Minor Benefit
Webbed Fingers - You gain a small amount of webbing between your fingers and toes.  You gain a swim speed equal to your walking speed.  If you already have a swim speed that is equal to or greater than your walking speed, add 10 feet to the swim speed you have.

Minor Detriment
Feast of the Dead - When in the presence of a humanoid corpse, make a Wisdom save with a DC of 15.  If you fail, you suffer some sort of visible effect that makes people think you want to eat the body (which you likely don’t actually want to do).  Maybe your skin pales, or you grow fangs, or maybe you just look ravenous.  Regardless, you suffer disadvantage on all Charisma skill checks while you can see the body.
